Topographic Analysis of Alto Mayo and Cordillera de Colán Protected Areas
Slope and elevation analysis of two protected areas in northern Peru.
Full document
RStudio R






The Bosque de Protección Alto Mayo (BPAM) and Santuario Nacional Cordillera de Colán (SNCC) are two protected areas in northern Peru that form part of the Abiseo-Cóndor-Kutukú transboundary conservation corridor. Using R, I processed a 30m Copernicus DEM to generate a classified slope map and an elevation histogram for a study area encompassing both protected areas and a 20 km buffer zone. Over 81% of the area has steep to very steep slopes (>15%), with a highly variable elevation range of 332–3,998 m.a.s.l. (SD = 761 m), reflecting the complex Andean-Amazonian transition landscape.


Elevation distribution across the study area. Values range from 332 to 3,998 m.a.s.l. with high variability (SD = 761 m). The positively skewed distribution — with most cells concentrated below 1,000 m — reflects the dominance of mid-elevation Andean slopes transitioning into lowland Amazon forest.

title: About
text:
I am an Environmental Engineer from Trujillo, Peru, with over six years of experience in environmental management, GIS, and spatial analysis.
My work spans environmental impact assessment and monitoring across agriculture, energy, and production sectors, as well as biological monitoring fieldwork in the Tambopata National Reserve and vegetation mapping of the Colombian páramo ecosystem with FUNDA. I am currently a GIS Intern with the Ceiba Foundation for Tropical Conservation in Ecuador, where I work on land cover change analysis and biodiversity spatial data.
My current focus is forest monitoring, land-use change detection, and building reproducible spatial workflows in R and Google Earth Engine for conservation applications. This portfolio documents that work.
Alongside technical work, I have a background in environmental communication and graphic design through volunteer roles with NGOs, where I developed visual content and campaigns to make environmental issues accessible to broader audiences.
